title: Annotatio IV §.XVI open: Bernard of Clairvaux follows Berengar — food of mind; spiritual exhibition
pass_a_gloss: §. XVI. The footsteps of Berengar, piously deceased around the end of the XIth Age, in teaching concerning the Sacred Supper, BERNARD ABBOT OF CLAIRVAUX, easily Prince of Ascetic Writers in his time, followed near the very BEGINNING OF THE XIIth AGE — of which the witnesses are two most ample Sermons undoubtedly attributed to him, one On the Purification of Mary, the other On S. Martin, written and delivered. In the former you will read that Christ’s body in the Mystery (of the Supper) is food of the mind, not of the belly, and therefore is not eaten corporally; for as it is food, so also it is understood to be eaten. But in the latter: That even to this day the same flesh of Christ is exhibited to us, but spiritually indeed, not corporally.
pass_b_english: §.XVI: near the opening of the XIIth age, BERNARD OF CLAIRVAUX — then prince of ascetic writers — walks Berengar’s footsteps on the Sacred Supper.
Two sermons (Purification of Mary; S. Martin): Christ’s body in the Mystery is food of the mind, not the belly — not eaten corporally; the same flesh is exhibited spiritually, not corporally.
source_text: §. XVI. Berengarii, circa finem Seculi XI. piè demortui vestigia, docendo de S. Cœna, legit Asceticorum Scriptorum suo tempore facilè Princeps BERNHARDUS ABBAS CLARÆVALLENSIS sub ipsum ferè SECULI XIImi INITIUM, quo de testes sunt amplissimæ, binæ ejus Conciones indubitatò illi tribuendæ, altera de purificatione Mariæ, de S. Martino altera conscripta habitaque. In priori legeris, quòd Christi corpus in Mysterio (Cœnæ) cibus mentis sit, non ventris, proinde corporaliter non manducetur, sicut enim cibus est, ita & comedi intelligitur. In posteriori verò: Quod usque hodie eadem caro Christi, nobis, sed spiritualiter utique, non corporaliter exhibeatur.
